variants.headline: Party leader faces a public scandal
variants.sub: The leader of {party}, {leader}, is the subject of a newly revealed scandal.
variants.body:
A scandal concerning {leader}, the leader of {party}, has come to light. The revelation makes political trust an immediate subject of public attention. An assessment of {target} must distinguish that known fact from unreported details about the conduct involved, its cause or any proceedings that might follow.

Our political principles ought to survive the discomfort of applying them to leaders. Trust is not a private asset belonging to a party hierarchy. It concerns the people asked to give their support, and they deserve an argument about responsibility that does not depend on convenient invention.

In our judgment, {target} does not deserve confidence in this matter. Political trust requires a demanding standard, and the scandal is an appropriate occasion for a distinctly critical assessment. Political principle should remain visible when judgment becomes less comfortable.
